title: Deployment Cursor: Weekly Spotlight - May 2028
content:
Purpose:
Quick weekly snapshot from the private deployments team — focusing on VPC/on-prem installs currently in flight, lingering customer blockers, and near-term runbook changes we need to ship. This doc is deliberately terse: callouts, diagnostics snippets, and action owners for fast handoffs during on-call/field shifts.

Highlights this week:
- Two large on-prem installs (Customer: RadiantHealth, Acadia AI) progressed to post-install smoke; RadiantHealth still has an intermittent KV cache pressure symptom.
- VPC install template 3.1 patch released to staging; includes new NTP/chrony precheck and graceful kubelet restart strategy.
- Network team validated MTU mismatch triggering TCP retransmits in 3 customer networks — an interim workaround (jumbo-frame alert) added to playbook.

Current installs (brief):
1) RadiantHealth (onprem) — lead: Diego
   - Status: Post-deploy smoke failing intermittently (10% of requests see 500 within 5-10m windows).
   - Observations: During failures, node-level memory climbs briefly then GC churn leads to tokenization service restart. KV cache hit rate drops to 40%.
   - Recent actions: Captured heapdumps and pprof at 2028-05-05 14:12 UTC; diag trace ID RH-2028-05-05-1412.
   - Next: Diego to run targeted traffic with 1.5x token length distribution to reproduce; try pruning large prefixes from cache and set cache_eviction_threshold=0.65.
   - Blocker: Customer firewall blocks outbound telemetry on port 443 -> need explicit allowlist for our metrics proxy (ticket JIRA-7812).

2) Acadia AI (VPC) — lead: Sina
   - Status: Install complete; sustained load test at 200qps succeeded except for 50ms variance on tails.
   - Observations: Tail latency correlated with DNS failover to secondary resolver when primary had transient drop.
   - Recent actions: Short-term: pin /etc/resolv.conf ordering and add nscd cache; Long-term: recommend in-console resolver healthcheck.
   - Next: Post-deploy A/B of pinned resolver vs. system resolver next Tue.

3) Small pilot: Atelier Legal (edge onprem) — lead: Priya
   - Status: Stuck at storage mount validation (NFS v4 acl mismatch).
   - Workaround: Mount with single-user fallback flag; storage team investigating ACL sync tool (JIRA-7830).

Cross-cutting issues and diagnostics notes:
- Network MTU mismatch: Found on three customer environments. Symptoms: slow start, retransmits, and heavy tail latency. Repro script: iperf3 tests with varying MSS; posted results in gitlab CI artifact (see linked_artifacts). Temporary mitigation: set --net-mtu 1436 on host docs.
- Telemetry egress: Some enterprise customers block our metrics proxy; we need to ship an encrypted push-over-443 mode (opt-in) in next minor.
- KV cache eviction: Observed two patterns — (a) large single-key prefixes that bloat LRU, (b) transient bursts from long-context chat sessions. Suggested config knobs: cache_eviction_threshold, max_prefix_weight, and enable_adaptive_eviction.

Action items and owners (this sprint):
- Diego: reproduce RH memory/GC with synthetic load + patch to cache_eviction_threshold; target complete by 2028-05-11.
- Priya: coordinate with storage eng to get ACL fix and validate NFS mounts for Atelier Legal by 2028-05-12.
- Sina: run resolver A/B test with Acadia and report metrics (p50/p95/p99) on 2028-05-15.
- Asha: draft small RFC for encrypted telemetry over 443 and circulate to network/security by 2028-05-09.
- Platform: prepare 3.1.1 hotfix with NTP precheck + kubelet restart safepoint; aim to cut by 2028-05-13.

Known risks (short):
- Customer zones with strict egress rules will continue to block our default telemetry path; this increases MTTR for incidents.
- Air-gapped installs: we still have manual steps in the transfer sequence that add ~6-8 hours to handoffs; need to automate checksum and bundle signing to reduce friction.

Runbook tweaks proposed (quick list):
- Add MTU diagnostic subsection (iperf3 commands, expected thresholds, remediation steps).
- Add NTP precheck before node join (if clock skew > 2s fail with clear action).
- Document telemetry fallback (443 push) and explicit customer sign-off checkbox in provisioning form.
- Add a short snippet for capturing heapdump/pprof with a single command for field engineers (include safe collection flags).

Meeting notes (weekly sync 2028-05-09):
- TL;DR: focus on three things — (1) reduce telemetry blind spots, (2) ship 3.1.1 hotfix, (3) prioritize RadiantHealth stability.
- Decision: enable adaptive_eviction for installs with memory-constrained nodes by default until we have kernel-level fixes. (Owner: platform)
- Concern raised by Support: customers are confused by two parallel resolver recommendations; Product to draft a single recommended network baseline doc by 2028-05-16.
- E2E plan: after 3.1.1 cut, run a canary cohort of 5 installs (mix of VPC and onprem) and monitor cost/latency/signal quality for 72 hours.

Notes to self / field hints:
- When customer reports "intermittent 500s", ask for timeline + full traceroute and tcpdump during window. Correlate with kubelet restart events in the node journal.
- Quick triage sequence: verify NTP -> verify MTU -> capture heap/profile -> verify telemetry egress.

Open questions / things to escalate:
- Do we want to enable encrypted-telemetry-by-default for enterprise tier? (Product + Security input requested).
- Is there appetite to include automated ACL sync tool as part of the install bundle for customers with managed storage? (Ask storage eng).

Appendix (short command snippets):
- Check MTU: ip link show dev eth0 ; ping -M do -s 1400 <peer-ip>
- Heapdump: REDWOOD_DUMP_ON_SIGUSR2=1 kill -USR2 <pid> (collect off-host via scp)
- pprof: go tool pprof -http=:8080 /tmp/heap.pprof

If anything above needs re-prioritization, ping me in #priv-deploy or drop a comment inline. Will update this doc after Diego's repro attempt and platform hotfix cut.

-- Asha
